name_zh: 泰国·披耶·巴玛：学生起义与民主军事循环
name_en: Thailand Phibun: Student Uprising & Democracy Military Cycle
description_zh: 披耶·巴玛 (1897-1964) 泰国元帅总理 (1938-1944, 1948-1957)，1932年推翻绝对君主制建立立宪君主制，二战亲日倒向盟友，战后美国支持反共独裁，1973/1992学生起义推翻军政府，民主-军事循环至今。
description_en: Phibun Phahon (1897-1964) Thailand Field Marshal PM (1938-1944, 1948-1957), 1932 overthrew absolute monarchy established constitutional monarchy, WWII pro-Japan then switched to Allies, post-war US-backed anti-communist dictatorship, 1973/1992 student uprisings overthrew military juntas, democracy-military cycle continues.
reason_zh: 披耶代表泰国民主-军事循环的核心人物，展示了立宪君主制如何在军人政治、学生运动、美苏冷战博弈中反复震荡，至今未形成稳定民主巩固机制。
reason_en: Phibun represents Thailand democracy-military cycle core figure, demonstrating how constitutional monarchy oscillates among military politics, student movements, US-Soviet Cold War competition, still lacking stable democratic consolidation mechanism today.
steps_zh: 研究披耶早年军官与1932年立宪革命领袖角色
分析1938-1944首相期亲日政策与泰国收复领土
探讨1947年政变回归与美国反共军事援助
评估1957年萨立特政变下台与1973/1992学生起义循环
总结泰国民主军事循环至今未解的结构性困境
steps_en: Study Phibun early officer and 1932 constitutional revolution leader role
Analyze 1938-1944 PM pro-Japan policy and Thailand territorial recovery
Explore 1947 coup return and US anti-communist military aid
Evaluate 1957 Sarit coup ousting and 1973/1992 student uprising cycle
Summarize Thailand democracy-military cycle structural dilemma unresolved today
expected_zh: 理解泰国立宪君主制下军人政治与学生民主运动的反复博弈，掌握冷战地缘政治对东南亚民主化进程的深度塑造，评估泰国民主巩固的根本障碍。
expected_en: Understand Thai constitutional monarchy military politics and student democratic movement repeated game, grasp Cold War geopolitics deep shaping of Southeast Asian democratization, evaluate Thailand democratic consolidation fundamental obstacles.
case_zh: 1932 立宪革命；1938 首相；1944 辞职；1948 再任；1957 下台；1973/1992 学生起义循环。民主军事循环范式永存。
case_en: 1932 constitutional revolution; 1938 PM; 1944 resigned; 1948 re-PM; 1957 ousted; 1973/1992 student uprising cycle. Democracy military cycle paradigm endures.
cross_cultural_impact: Democracy-military cycle; constitutional monarchy; student uprisings; Cold War proxy
